summary: Dedicated capacity throughput collapse in us-west during scheduled snapshot causing autoscaler telemetry gap and noisy-neighbor-like GPU attach delays
description: Issue summary: Customer ClearVoice reported a ~6x p99 latency increase and 60% sustained throughput loss in their dedicated reserved pool (us-west) that started at 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC during our scheduled nightly snapshot window. Impact: customer-facing production traffic degraded; some requests returned 503/504 and many experienced attach timeouts. Initial triage suggested noisy-neighbor GPU contention, but telemetry shows an autoscaler telemetry gap and snapshotter-induced IO saturation coincident with a Sidecar version mismatch.
impact: Customer experiencing degraded throughput and elevated 5xx on dedicated reserved pool; business impact to ClearVoice’s data pipeline and SLA breach risk.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule snapshot sweep on reserved hosts in us-west during high prewarm traffic. 2) Deploy sidecar v1.9.2 to a subset of hosts while fleet runs v1.9.0 agent. 3) Run mixed short/long-stream workload pinned to gpt-large-v2 and observe allocator and attach latencies. 4) Watch autoscaler signals and snapshotter IO metrics.
observed_logs_and_metrics:
- allocator.attach.latency p95 -> 1.4s (baseline 120ms)
- gpu.attach.errors: spike from 0.01% to 4.3% during window
- host.io.utilization: NVMe read/write at 98% for snapshot shard activity
- autoscaler.telemetry.batch_rate: telemetry gap 02:39:40-02:43:10 UTC (ingestion dropped)
- serving-runtime kernel queue depth increased and unresolved prefetch waiters observed
- support dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/alloc/us-west-reserved?from=2026-03-10T02:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T03:00:00Z
initial_hypothesis: A combination of snapshotter IO saturation and a sidecar agent version skew caused high host IO, increasing GPU NVMe latency on several reserved hosts. The autoscaler relied on delayed metrics and briefly removed capacity (or failed to scale) resulting in attach contention and behavior that looked like noisy-neighbor GPU shortfall. The mismatch in sidecar caused partial telemetry ingestion, making the autoscaler misclassify the severity and delaying corrective scale-ups.
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed snapshot sweep coincident with customer report via scheduler logs.
- Found ~12 hosts reporting higher driver reclaim and intermittent NVMe stalls; kernel logs show repeated WARN: nvme_io_timeout on those hosts.
- Sidecar rollout history indicates 30% of reserved hosts were still on v1.9.0 while new snapshotter bump requires v1.9.2 for backpressure metrics.
- Autoscaler monitors (batch-rate, healthy-slots) had partial telemetry due to sidecar v1.9.0 not exposing new snapshot backpressure metric; ingestion pipeline dropped ~8% of telemetry events causing smoothing logic to compute an artificially lower backlog.
- Temporary autoscaler action at 02:41 UTC triggered a scaledown of ephemeral capacity then failed to re-attach expected GPUs because attach latencies had climbed, producing cascading fallback to lower-throughput model variants for some routes.
- Cross-referenced host IDs and found heavy IO correlated with snapshot shard writes from maintenance job MNT-2026-03-10-01. Link to host list: https://internal.redwood.ai/hosts/us-west/reserved/snapshot-2026-03-10 (internal)
customer_communication: - 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC: Notified ClearVoice that we detected a capacity disruption and opened an incident.\n- 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: Provided temporary routing to standby reserved pool in eu-west and enabled model fallback to gpt-medium-quant for latency-sensitive routes.\n- 2026-03-11 10:00 UTC: Sent post-incident status and next steps: prioritized host remediation and sidecar forced upgrade.
temporary_workaround: 1) Shifted ClearVoice traffic to standby reserved pool in eu-west for critical routes; 2) Applied aggressive per-tenant connection throttling on the us-west pool to reduce connection fanout and free batchers; 3) Disabled snapshot shard writes on affected hosts until NVMe cleanup completed.
long_term_fix_plan:
- Enforce sidecar version compatibility check in scheduler preflight; reject snapshot jobs on hosts with older sidecar.
- Add autoscaler fallback to increase capacity on telemetry gaps (if ingestion drops >5% over 30s, trigger protective scale-up).
- Introduce IO isolation for snapshotter shards (IOQoS) to avoid NVMe saturation during high-traffic windows.
- Add a canary policy for snapshotter/sidecar rollouts in reserved pools.
- Postmortem to be written under confluence page linked above and ownership assigned to infra/scheduler team.
resolution: In progress: hosts remediated, forced sidecar roll to v1.9.2 completed by 2026-03-11 03:20 UTC. NVMe kernel errors reduced and attach latencies returned to within 2x baseline after throttling and rebalancing. Autoscaler patch to detect ingestion gaps deployed to staging; rollout to prod scheduled 2026-03-15.
follow_up_tasks: Scheduler preflight: add sidecar-version check (owner: SRE squad)
